epics.title: Phaser procedural baseline and Chromium static smoke
epics.outcome: One Phaser version is selected, documented, and pinned across engine and tooling, and a Chromium-only local static build with deterministic code-native visuals and procedural chiptune audio runs without blocking errors while the accepted quality and accessibility initialization can be observed.
acceptanceCriteria: The smoke run initializes the accepted accessibility baseline: screen shake defaults to 40% or off, prefers-reduced-motion is honored, adjustable ball speed is represented as an available control hook, and visual-mirror controls are represented as available settings hooks; these values are captured in the run record.

epics.title: Core playable slice in Phaser
epics.outcome: A minimal core playable slice is produced in Phaser so that paddle, ball, block, basic collision/return, combo escalation visual, audio, and persistence hooks are observable within the first 10 seconds of active play.
acceptanceCriteria: Persistence hooks are observable as in-memory or local-storage state events during the run, and the run record reports the observed event stream rather than only static source review.

epics.title: Accessibility defaults and adjustable browser controls
epics.outcome: Accessibility defaults and adjustable controls are represented in UI and verified in a Chromium browser run, including screen-shake reduction, reduced-motion handling, ball speed adjustment, and user-controllable visual mirrors for audio.
acceptanceCriteria: No additional browser matrix, mobile certification, or real-device certification is introduced beyond the accepted Chromium-only verification.

epics.title: Procedural original chiptune layer and reactive stinger hooks
epics.outcome: Procedural original chiptune generation is verified as an engine-native approach, producing a loopable track layer structure with reactive stinger hooks, hash-bound provenance, declared project-use rights, and no external audio dependency required for this increment.
acceptanceCriteria: The implementation records hash-bound provenance and declared project-use rights for the original procedural audio output, using source/configuration/commit hashes rather than externally authored media provenance.

epics.title: Independent Chromium QA validation of the first increment
epics.outcome: The increment is validated independently by QA using browser startup, interaction observation, and accessibility walkthrough in Chromium, with Technical Director planning and review only.
acceptanceCriteria: QA runs the integrated Chromium candidate and records pass or fail evidence for startup, core gameplay observation, accessibility walkthrough, and procedural audio behavior using the shared browser scenario harness where required.
